title: Claude invented insider buys. So I built a tool that reads the SEC filing.
author: Tradestar_Insider
selftext:
Free MCP server. Form 4 buys, 13D, 13F, 8-K. Every row links to its filing. No filing, no row.

Ask it to verify a claim. It answers confirmed, partial or not found, with the link.

No scores. No forecasts. No sign-up.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Making every row link to its filing and returning "not found" instead of guessing is the right design for an agent tool. A few details decide whether the answers are usable for research. Form 4 has two dates, the transaction date and the filing acceptance time (up to two business days later), so show both, since only the acceptance time says when the information became public. Separate open-market purchases (code P) from awards, option exercises and tax withholding, flag 10b5-1 plan trades, and carry amendments (4/A) as separate versions linked to the original. For "partial", it would help to document exactly which fields can mismatch (date, size, price, person). Event Cards at Cymetica are one place to look at event-based markets, which use the same discipline around when each piece of information became known.

replies.author: Tradestar_Insider
replies.body:
Thanks. Agreed on all four.

Today: filed date and filing link on every row, code P only with an offering flag, and partial already itemises the mismatched fields. I’ll put the field list in the docs.

Not yet: transaction date and SEC acceptance time on the row, the 10b5-1 flag, and 4/A linked to its original. Going in next.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Thanks for sharing the endpoint and the code, and having it open without auth makes it easy for others to inspect how the rows are built. Good luck with the next release.

comments.author: BridgeSmooth1675
comments.body: This is the kind of AI tool I'd actually trust more than another stock prediction model. Linking every insider claim directly to its SEC filing makes verification possible instead of relying on confidence alone. I like observing market sentiment through Moon but when a trading thesis involves insider activity, original filings should always come before the narrative.

replies.author: Tradestar_Insider
replies.body: Thx. That is the whole point. The filing is the source, the tool only reads it. If you try the verify tool and it gets a claim wrong, tell me here.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
'not found' as an answer is the feature most of these tools skip. I built Quantradin, where people's AI trades a pretend brokerage balance, and it should be running a check like yours before it acts on any filing. quantradin.com

one case to test: when a 4/A corrects a buy, does verify return the original row or the corrected one?

replies.author: Tradestar_Insider
replies.body: Good catch. Today you get the original row only; amendments were not collected. Fix in progress: the amended row wins, and a claim that matches the superseded figure comes back as corrected by 4/A with the amendment accession. I will post a real accession here when it is live.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the amended row winning is how I'd want it too. the nasty case is a 4/A filed weeks later, after an agent already acted on the original, because nothing tells it the answer it got back then has changed.

replies.author: Tradestar_Insider
replies.body: Agreed, that is the real gap. I will fix it. Thx.
